applicability: Checking the exact loaded-pad shear threshold before coupling contact to an articulated actuator
Separating maintained contact from actual tangential holding capacity
claim: In the exact certified L3.1 free unary pad fixture with reconstructed 59.6 newtons of normal support and authored friction 0.6, the centered pad holds through 34 newtons of imposed shear and slides at 36 newtons, producing a measured breakaway-ratio bracket of 0.57047 to 0.60403 inside the accepted L1 friction envelope.

evidence.certification_claim_boundary: This campaign can certify only the exact L3.0-L3.2 free unary loaded-pad observations named by the source-pinned programs. The force-controlled carriage is an explicit apply_force boundary and not a rail; centered normal loading, loaded shear breakaway, predicted contact-pressure edge migration, and rocking retain their declared fixture, load, geometry, material, timestep, and solver scopes. It establishes no general contact wrench, per-contact or per-foot load allocation, articulated load-bearing limb, standing, bracing, fall arrest, getting up, gait, walking, accepted knowledge, or automatic creature guidance.

program.claim_scope: The declared free unary pad retains reconstructed 59.6 N normal support and brackets friction-0.6 shear breakaway between 34 and 36 N inside the accepted L1 friction envelope.

failure_boundaries: Continuous contact does not by itself establish stable support or bracing
The result is one free unary pad and does not allocate load among multiple feet, toes, or contact manifolds
No articulated load-bearing limb, standing, bracing, fall arrest, getting up, gait, or walking is established
mechanism: Whole-system reconstruction retains the aggregate normal-load denominator while post-step pad kinematics distinguish held and sliding cells. The measured transition is checked against the already accepted L1 friction interval instead of inferring friction from contact presence alone.
